channel.title: Security Briefing — weownit.net
channel.description: Cybersecurity news and research: vulnerabilities, ransomware, identity, cloud and software supply chains. Reported facts, practical checks and remediation you can validate.

item.title: FortiOS management HTTPS denial of service: CVE-2026-106174
item.description: FortiOS 8.0.0 and 7.6.4–7.6.6 have an improper-locking flaw that can let an unauthenticated attacker with network access disrupt the HTTPS management interface. This is an availability issue; public exploitation is not established by this advisory.

item.title: Actively exploited Cisco ASA/FTD SSL VPN denial of service: CVE-2026-76418
item.description: Cisco reports active exploitation of a flaw that can reload ASA/FTD devices when reachable remote-access SSL VPN uses secondary authentication in the affected tunnel group. It is a service-availability risk, not evidence of data theft.

item.title: Check Point Quantum Security Management pre-auth compromise: CVE-2026-93616
item.description: Check Point reported limited exploitation of a pre-authentication path-traversal flaw in Quantum Security Management that can lead to arbitrary script execution. This is an older but high-priority carry-forward item, not a new November discovery.

item.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support: exploited origin-validation flaw (CVE-2026-102764)
item.description: CVE-2026-102764 allowed unauthorized file operations against affected Remote Support appliances. BeyondTrust and investigators report attacks before disclosure; patching alone cannot exclude a prior compromise.

item.title: PHP2Shell: exposed applications and infrastructure management
item.description: From application runtimes to management interfaces: confirm the affected product before choosing the fix.

item.title: From VPN to ransomware: review GlobalProtect access
item.description: Unit 42 research updated in October connects VPN exploitation with ransomware and access to virtual infrastructure.

item.title: MythicRatatoskr: command and control hidden in a mesh network
item.description: New research on a 2025 incident: what to examine when the real communication destination is not a conventional C2 domain.

item.title: Gheist: when a GitHub token exposes deployment secrets
item.description: CI/CD abuse can reach service and infrastructure credentials. Deleting the workflow does not close the incident.

item.title: Stolen Microsoft 365 sessions: why a password reset is not enough
item.description: Token replay and identity persistence: review sessions, devices, MFA methods and email rules.

item.title: From a fake installer to Akira ransomware
item.description: A DFIR case study follows a July 2025 intrusion through to ransomware.
